newsitem.title: GERMANY: KJS intends to keep lead in German coffee market.
newsitem.headline: KJS intends to keep lead in German coffee market.

text.p: Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS), part of the U.S. food group Philip Morris, said it did not feel threatened in its coffee market activities by the planned purchase of Eduscho GmbH & Co by Tchibo Holding AG.
A company spokesman quoted managing director Bernhard Huber as saying, "We are the German market leader and are firmly committed to maintaining and extending this role."
KJS in October had a 30.7 percent volume share in Germany's coffee market, it said.
This was up from 29.8 percent in September and 29.6 percent in August.
Germany, the world's second largest coffee consumer after the U.S., in 1995 consumed 564,000 tonnes of green coffee.
Tchibo, Germany's number two, would not give a precise market share figure, but said its share was currently declining.
Eduscho said it last had 11 percent and its position varied between third, fourth and fifth place, depending on the competition.
The KJS spokesman said if added up in theory, Tchibo and Eduscho may represent 27 or 28 percent at the very best.
But both Tchibo and Eduscho have stressed there would be no merger but the two firms would continue to be run as separate entities.
